questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn you about road conditions. This sign tells you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: A vehicle coming toward you has its high beams on at night, making it hard to see. You should:

options.text: Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the circumstances are.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must be able to see clearly through all your vehicle's windows. Before driving, remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if the:

options.text: Vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
Yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is prohibited from both directions.
Passing is permitted from both directions.
Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a dashed line and a solid line, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross the center to pass. Traffic next to the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction of travel.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no traffic from either direction may cross the center to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a traffic signal that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and look before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Right turn on red light permitted with caution.
All traffic must turn right at next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves.

questions.question: Which lane must you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down before curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and roads with animals or pedestrians. You can drive slower than the speed limit for safety, but never faster.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards patrolling parking lots.
Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must follow signs and instructions from flaggers. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks carrying hazardous materials, etc.).
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Check for trains from both directions. Also watch for vehicles like school buses and hazmat trucks that must always stop at railroad crossings.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to high beam.
Turn your lights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: If you see flooded roads ahead, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may hide dangers even if it looks shallow. Find a different route instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: General warning signs.
Construction and maintenance warning signs.
Regulatory signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always be prepared to yield to prevent a collision, even if the rules say you have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more space to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not cut in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to return to your lane sooner. Return to your lane only when you see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: How can you help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a steep hill.
Speed up before entering curves and slow down after exiting them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left side of the cab.
Both on the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The truck driver cannot see your car behind them. You also cannot see traffic ahead if you drive too close behind the truck. The driver cannot see you if you cannot see their face in their mirror.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing them.
Cars coming toward them.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming cars driving straight. You can only turn left when it is safe and will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Have the ability to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts is false?

options.text: They hold you in place during a collision.
They are not necessary if your vehicle has an airbag.
They keep you from being thrown from the vehicle during an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not necessary if your vehicle has an airbag.
questions.explanation: State law requires you to wear seat belts even if your vehicle has airbags. Airbags protect you from hitting the steering wheel, dashboard, and windshield. However, they do not protect you if your vehicle is hit from the side or rear or if it rolls over. Airbags alone cannot keep you behind the wheel in these situations.
